latest_release.body:
## 🏎️ Performance Improvements

## Faster dependency discovery in large repositories

`run --all`, and `find` or `list` with `--dependencies`, are faster in large repositories, including ones with no `dependency` blocks. The time spent linking units to their dependencies now grows linearly with the number of units instead of quadratically.

In [benchmarks](https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/blob/main/internal/discovery/benchmark_relationship_test.go) on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, discovering units and their dependencies in a generated repository of 10-unit dependency chains:

| units | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 0.63ms | 0.63ms |
| 100 | 5.2ms | 5.0ms |
| 1,000 | 56ms | 47ms |
| 10,000 | 1.32s | 443ms |

At 10,000 units, memory allocated during discovery dropped from 8.6 GB to 1.9 GB.

## Faster discovery with dependent filters

Terragrunt wastes less time resolving symlinks in discovery. Dependent filters, such as `--filter '...vpc'` were able to reduce the number of wasted syscalls to resolve symlinks, improving dependent discovery.

On a repository of 1,024 units, discovery with a dependent filter took 30% less time from the repository root and 47% less time from the target unit's directory on an M3 Max. It also allocated 12-16% less memory.

## Faster discovery of dependencies

Discovery prepared to read a `terragrunt.stack.hcl` in every directory named by a `dependency` or `dependencies` block, even when the directory was a unit. It now does that work only when the stack file exists.

In [benchmarks](https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/blob/main/internal/discovery/benchmark_dependents_test.go) on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, selecting the dependents of a unit that every other unit depends on, run from that unit's directory:

| units | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 2.9ms | 2.3ms |
| 100 | 118ms | 86ms |
| 1,000 | 11.1s | 8.0s |

At 1,000 units, memory allocated during discovery dropped from 26.7 GiB to 10.3 GiB.

## 💡 Tips Added

## `inputs-read-not-tracked` — Points at files read in `inputs` that reading filters miss

Terragrunt does not track a file read in `inputs`. A unit with this configuration is not selected by `--filter 'reading=config.yml'` or by a Git filter when `config.yml` changes:

```hcl
# terragrunt.hcl

inputs = {
  message = yamldecode(file("config.yml")).message
}
```

The same applies to `inputs` in an `autoinclude` block of a stack file.

Commands that track reads, such as `run --all` with a reading or Git filter and `find --reading`, now print the `inputs-read-not-tracked` tip pointing at each such read:

```text
TIP (inputs-read-not-tracked): Terragrunt does not track files read in `inputs`, so reading and Git filters miss the units and stacks that read them.

Untracked file read in `inputs`
 --> app/terragrunt.hcl:4:24
  |
4 |   message = yamldecode(file("config.yml")).message
  |                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Read the file in `locals` and reference the local here.

Untracked file read in an `autoinclude` block's `inputs`
 --> live/terragrunt.stack.hcl:16:29
   |
16 |       policy = templatefile("policy.json.tftpl", { role_arn = dependency.iam.outputs.role_arn })
   |                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = Mark the template as read with `mark_as_read` in the stack's `locals`, then pass the local as the path here.

See https://docs.terragrunt.com/features/filter/attributes#reading-based-expressions
```

See [Reading-Based Expressions](https://docs.terragrunt.com/features/filter/attributes#reading-based-expressions). Suppress the tip with `--no-tip inputs-read-not-tracked` or `--no-tips`.

## 🔒 Strict Controls Added

## `cas-source-inside-stack` strict control

A `unit` or `stack` block with `update_source_with_cas` could set a source inside the directory of its own stack file, e.g. a catalog with its stack at the root and its units under `units/`:

# Terragrunt

[![Maintained by Gruntwork.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/maintained%20by-gruntwork.io-%235849a6.svg)](https://gruntwork.io/?ref=repo_terragrunt)
[![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt)
[![GoDoc](https://godoc.org/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt?status.svg)](https://godoc.org/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt)
![OpenTofu Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/tofu-%3E%3D1.6.0-blue.svg)
![Terraform Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/tf-%3E%3D0.12.0-blue.svg)

Terragrunt is a flexible orchestration tool that allows Infrastructure as Code written in [OpenTofu](https://opentofu.org)/[Terraform](https://www.terraform.io) to scale.

Please see the following for more info, including install instructions and complete documentation:

* [Terragrunt Website](https://terragrunt.com)
* [Getting started with Terragrunt](https://docs.terragrunt.com/getting-started/quick-start/)
* [Terragrunt Documentation](https://docs.terragrunt.com/)
* [Terragrunt Scale](https://docs.terragrunt.com/terragrunt-scale/)
* [Contributing to Terragrunt](https://docs.terragrunt.com/community/contributing)
* [Commercial Support](https://gruntwork.io/support/)

## Join the Discord!

Join [our community](https://discord.com/invite/YENaT9h8jh) for discussions, support, and contributions:
